front.title: Revocation Closure and Authority Epochs for Agent Delegation

abstract.t:
Automated agents can exercise OAuth-derived authority through delegated credentials, child agents, asynchronous work, and operations spanning multiple administrative domains. Invalidating an individual token does not necessarily establish that the authority represented by that token can no longer cause a new consequential operation.
This document defines authority epochs, delegation-lineage requirements, admission fencing, and revocation-closure states for OAuth-based agent delegation. It distinguishes token invalidation from authority closure and specifies that unresolved in-scope state produces UNKNOWN or PARTIAL rather than CLOSED. The profile composes with OAuth Token Revocation, Token Exchange, Token Introspection, proof-of-possession mechanisms, Transaction Tokens, and workload- identity systems such as WIMSE.
